_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local nodes for band2_stone_and_root. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order harvest nodes are added to the scene tree. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 2000-2999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

nodes._comment_sd16: SD16, spec §3 Band 2 and §10: the Rootstone deposits on the Old Quarry's floor, reachable only past the South Bridge. Pickaxe-gated the same way stone is -- `gathered_with` on the ITEM (data/items/items.json), never on the node, so the rule lives in one place and a bare-handed player is told what they need rather than silently refused (OF20). Five deposits at 2 each: enough that a first visit is worth the walk, few enough that the quarry is a place you go back to rather than a vending machine. Amounts and positions TUNABLE; every one of them stands on the quarry pad (terrain_playground.json `flats`, centre [23,158] r8) and is clear of both foundations, the prop cluster and the conduit head by at least 4m so no two interact prompts contest.
nodes._comment_ow5d: OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: all five rootstone deposits below move by the same uniform (+377,+1642) offset as the quarry itself (old anchor (23,158) -> new (400,1800), see old_quarry.json), preserving their relative layout on the quarry floor exactly.
nodes.label: Prise out rootstone
Prise out rootstone
nodes._why: hard against the quarry's own cut face, where the working stopped

nodes._comment_ow5d: OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: all five ironwood nodes below move by the same uniform (-490,+2610) offset as the Burrow Warrens' `site.at` (70,-140) -> (-420,2470), preserving their relative layout around the mouth exactly. BAND2-63-WARRENS then moved the cave again, (-420,2470) -> (-357,2610), because the OW5D site could not be walked through (burrow_warrens.json's `_comment_resiting`); these five moved with it by that same (+63,+140) -- and then were RE-ARRANGED, because the blind visual pass found what a uniform translation had done: one ironwood stood inside the knoll, and three more stood in the doorway corridor, the nearest 8.5m dead in front of the mouth. The frame the critic saw was a full-canopy red tree filling the cave entrance. They are now a stand ringing the site at 34-46m, 26m or more off the doorway axis and outside the authored clearing, so the player walks past ironwood on the way in instead of through it.
nodes.label: Fell an ironwood

nodes._comment_mq2b_spoil: MQ2B. The ridge between the quarry (400,1800) and the ranger camp spur (-150,2210) had no gatherable at all -- 410m of spine with nothing to reach for, the longest uncovered stretch on the band's western half. docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 5's own words for this band are 'quarried faces, spoil heaps'; ordinary stone read through that phrase rather than inventing a new material. Near the quarry_rim_overlook loop's own rejoin (330,1950), just off the spine.
nodes.label: Prise loose stones
Prise loose stones
nodes._why: second of the pair, short of the ranger camp spur's own fork at (-150,2210) -- a beat every 150-250m per the macro-layout's own density budget, not one lonely rock in the middle of 410m

nodes._comment_mq2b_ridge: MQ2B. Past the Warrens (-420,2470) the spine runs another ~710m to the band's own end (0,3180) with only the warren_undertrail loop's rejoin (-180,2730) on it -- the 'deeper oak forest' section 5 names for this band, read as gatherable wood the same way the spoil heaps above read as stone. Near the spine's own (-40,2840).
nodes.label: Gather deadwood
Gather deadwood
nodes._why: second of the pair, between the undertrail rejoin and the band's own end at (0,3180) so the last kilometre before the River Lock is not empty ground

nodes._comment_mq2b_round4: MQ2B, OPS15 blind-critic round 3->4. Two rounds of critique named the same thing from two different angles: 'no secondary ground dressing' and '85-95% flat, undetailed grass' in the stretches BETWEEN named landmarks. `harvest.json`'s own coordinator guidance is to spend entries on 'named nodes, ore, berries' rather than wood/stone (that's the scatter's job now). Berries, band1's own model/scale convention (Bush_Common_Flowers.gltf @ 1.2), placed in the trailpup/meadowhart stretch that had nothing between the South Bridge and the quarry.
nodes.label: Pick berries
Pick berries
nodes._why: second of the pair, close enough to the first to read as one thicket rather than two coincidences -- EV7-clusters-fix's own finding about touching vs scattered reads

nodes.label: Pick berries
nodes._why: the late-ridge stretch past the Warrens, beside the deadwood node (order 2004) and the night-gated duskhush spawn -- same reasoning as the pair above, ported to the band's other bare stretch

nodes._comment_camp: BAND2-63, prompt 61's camp-siting checklist: a field camp wants 'nearby basic wood/stone/fiber availability'. The `ranger_camp` clearing (vegetation.json order 2001, -259,2256.5) had none within 250m -- the nearest stone was the order 2002 pair, 300m+ back down the spur. A wood node right at the camp means a player who stops here to build a bed does not have to leave the clearing to feed it.
nodes.label: Gather deadwood
